Use Tier 3: combine the original binary-history MultVAE with a separately trained SASRec through an equal-weight rank ensemble. The supplied results suggest complementary strengths: SASRec achieved Electronics HR@10 of 0.420 versus MultVAE’s 0.355, while MultVAE achieved CDs_and_Vinyl HR@10 of 0.680 versus SASRec’s 0.480. Recency weighting reduced macro HR@10 to 0.5212, so this experiment will preserve full-history collaborative information and add a dedicated sequence model rather than reweight the VAE input.

Modify data_processing_and_feature_engineering, model_design, and training_evaluation. Keep MultVAE’s original deduplicated binary histories and give SASRec the original ordered histories, using only the supplied training split for both models. Train the two models separately for each of the four categories, retaining their existing architectures, objectives, and hyperparameters so the ensemble is the single experimental change. During prediction, score every supplied candidate with both trained models, convert each score vector to normalized descending ranks with average ranks for ties, and return the negative mean rank so larger outputs remain better. Fix the blend at equal weights across all categories without searching category-specific coefficients.

Select each component checkpoint using fixed validation HR@10, then evaluate the combined predictor on the same 200 users and 99 unique negatives per category with evaluation seed 42. Update the predictor writer to load both checkpoints by dataset_name and share the exact ranking implementation with local validation. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and sequential single-GPU training within the remaining budget; print the measured macro HR@10 as Final Validation Score and leave held-out prediction execution to the host. This tests whether combining sequential and collaborative rankings overcomes their individual limitations; improvement remains an empirical question.
